knowledgeItems.title: IntraWeb 17 FE is positioned as a visual web frontend IDE in VS Code
knowledgeItems.summary: The current FE page presents IntraWeb 17 FE as a complete visual web front-end development environment integrated with Visual Studio Code, supporting JavaScript and TypeScript.

knowledgeItems.title: Current FE page is explicitly a beta program
knowledgeItems.summary: The product page labels the FE offer as a beta program and identifies the current line as IntraWeb 17 FE v17.0, build 2026.04. Treat beta status as part of product context when writing claims.

knowledgeItems.title: One project can target web, WordPress, PWA, Android and iOS
knowledgeItems.summary: The current product page explicitly lists deployment to the web, use inside WordPress, and packaging paths for PWA, Android and iOS app stores.

knowledgeItems.title: IntraWeb 17 One separates frontend and backend and wires them together
knowledgeItems.summary: The product page describes IntraWeb 17 One as creating one application while separating frontend and backend and wiring the two automatically to reduce glue and integration work.

knowledgeItems.title: Local and offline development is part of the product positioning
knowledgeItems.summary: The product page emphasizes development inside VS Code with 100% offline work and no cloud dependency as a core toolchain characteristic.

knowledgeItems.title: Native debugging and normal source-control workflows are explicit product claims
knowledgeItems.summary: The FE page highlights native debugging together with Git and SVN workflows as part of the developer-controlled toolchain.

knowledgeItems.title: Generated output remains developer-owned
knowledgeItems.summary: The product page stresses that IntraWeb 17 FE is not hosted SaaS and that generated output remains available to the developer to inspect, host and deploy.

knowledgeItems.title: The native designer puts IWML, components, canvas and properties into one workflow
knowledgeItems.summary: The product page presents a native visual designer where IWML, components, the visual canvas and properties are handled as one frontend-building workflow.

knowledgeItems.title: Official Guess example reports a compact IntraWeb output
knowledgeItems.summary: The current product comparison reports the IntraWeb Guess example at 31.3 KB, 44.0 KB on disk, 15 files and 0 folders. This is an Atozed product-page example, not an independent benchmark.
knowledgeItems.sourceSection: IntraWeb FE vs React / Vue / Angular

knowledgeItems.title: Official product page compares the Guess example with React
knowledgeItems.summary: For the same product-page comparison, Atozed shows a React project folder at 39.9 MB, 44.2 MB on disk, 2,307 files and 223 folders. Any public comparison should identify this as the official example and re-check competitor setup before publication.

knowledgeItems.title: Official product page compares the Guess example with Vue
knowledgeItems.summary: Atozed shows the compared Vue project at 37.3 MB, 38.4 MB on disk, 737 files and 139 folders. Treat it as product-page evidence that needs current competitor verification before external publication.

knowledgeItems.title: Official product page compares the Guess example with Angular
knowledgeItems.summary: Atozed shows the compared Angular project at 230 MB, 262 MB on disk, 22,746 files and 2,340 folders. It is useful as an official comparison angle, not as a universal benchmark.

knowledgeItems.title: WordPress Custom HTML is shown as a direct integration path
knowledgeItems.summary: The product page demonstrates designing and publishing an IntraWeb block, adding a WordPress Custom HTML block, and loading the published app inside the WordPress page.

knowledgeItems.title: Current documentation describes IW17 as a structured component-based web platform
knowledgeItems.summary: The current introduction describes IntraWeb 17 as a platform for interactive web applications with structured UI definitions, organized application logic and dynamic browser content.

knowledgeItems.title: The VS Code extension is the documented development front door
knowledgeItems.summary: The current introduction says development is supported through a Visual Studio Code extension for creating, editing and running IntraWeb applications.

knowledgeItems.title: Current docs explicitly link Telegram and YouTube
knowledgeItems.summary: The IntraWeb 17 introduction links the IntraWeb17 Telegram community and the IntraWeb A2Z YouTube channel as official resources.

knowledgeItems.title: Create a new JavaScript or TypeScript project from the VS Code extension
knowledgeItems.summary: The extension UI can create a new project, select JavaScript or TypeScript, choose a name/location and open the generated project directly in VS Code.
knowledgeItems.sourceSection: Quick Start > Main Features of IntraWeb 17 Extension > New Project

knowledgeItems.title: A generated project starts with HTML, IWML, logic and IntraWeb.json
knowledgeItems.summary: The current extension documentation lists an HTML wrapper, Index.iwml, JavaScript/TypeScript logic and IntraWeb.json as the initial project files.
knowledgeItems.sourceSection: Quick Start > Main Features of IntraWeb 17 Extension > New Project

knowledgeItems.title: The extension can create demo projects for learning by example
knowledgeItems.summary: The current extension docs expose a Demo Project flow where a language and demo are selected and the generated demo opens directly in VS Code.
knowledgeItems.sourceSection: Quick Start > Main Features of IntraWeb 17 Extension > Demo Project

knowledgeItems.title: New Page generates the page files and updates launch configuration
knowledgeItems.summary: The VS Code extension can create a new page folder with its required files and update launch.json so the page can be launched and debugged.
knowledgeItems.sourceSection: Quick Start > Main Features of IntraWeb 17 Extension > New Page

knowledgeItems.title: IWML can be opened visually or edited as text
knowledgeItems.summary: The extension documentation exposes context actions to open IWML in the graphical designer, edit the IWML source directly, and set a page for launch.
knowledgeItems.sourceSection: Quick Start > Main Features of IntraWeb 17 Extension > Context Menu Features

knowledgeItems.title: IWML Runner is a fast path to launch an application
knowledgeItems.summary: The current Run guide describes opening an IWML file with IWML Runner to launch the application in the browser, alongside a normal web-server path.
knowledgeItems.sourceSection: Quick Start > Run > via IWML Runner

knowledgeItems.title: IWML is the core page description
knowledgeItems.summary: The Run guide describes IWML as the core of an IntraWeb 17 page and compares the role of an IWML file to a Delphi DFM for the web.

knowledgeItems.title: IWCL renders IWML into HTML in the browser
knowledgeItems.summary: The current Run guide explains that IWML is transformed into browser HTML by the IW Component Library. The reference documentation also describes IWCL as handling rendering and communication with server-side or REST components.

knowledgeItems.title: An HTML loader starts the IntraWeb runtime and page loading process
knowledgeItems.summary: The documentation explains that browsers do not consume IWML directly and use an HTML loader to load IntraWeb libraries and the IWML page. Separate loader documentation describes an internal loader and customizable loader HTML.

knowledgeItems.title: Debug-only files can be omitted from a simple static deployment path
knowledgeItems.summary: The Run guide distinguishes source/debug artifacts from the smaller file set needed for a non-debug deployment of the documented TypeScript example.

knowledgeItems.title: The documented architecture separates browser logic from the Delphi server path
knowledgeItems.summary: The Run documentation explains the current TypeScript/browser path and the intended Delphi server integration, including use of Delphi as a REST server in the documented workflow.

knowledgeItems.title: IWML supports one-way and two-way data binding
knowledgeItems.summary: The IWML data-binding reference explicitly supports one-way and two-way binding to objects, including data obtained and updated through REST.

knowledgeItems.title: Binding sources include HTTP, Data, Page, Prop, Rows, This and URL
knowledgeItems.summary: The current data-binding reference lists multiple source types, making each source family a possible focused tutorial or short-form explanation.

knowledgeItems.title: IWML Markdown supports formatting, extensible tags and bindings
knowledgeItems.summary: The Markdown reference documents formatting tags, custom tags and data-binding expressions that can be embedded in Markdown text.

knowledgeItems.title: IWCL is the common rendering library for IntraWeb language editions
knowledgeItems.summary: The IWCL reference describes it as the component library that renders IWML to HTML and handles communication with IntraWeb server components, user handlers or REST servers.

knowledgeItems.title: Layouts and cells are first-class parts of the IWML model
knowledgeItems.summary: The existing IW17 documentation structure includes dedicated layout and cell concepts, making UI composition a distinct reusable knowledge branch instead of mixing it into generic tutorials.

knowledgeItems.title: Controls and component behavior form a separate knowledge area
knowledgeItems.summary: The IW17 documentation treats visual controls and component behavior as distinct reference material. This supports dedicated content around controls rather than one catch-all feature category.

knowledgeItems.title: External/loadable UI libraries are part of the documented component ecosystem
knowledgeItems.summary: The documentation structure includes loadable libraries and integrations, which can be broken into focused content around individual UI/data libraries instead of a single integrations post.

knowledgeItems.title: Custom control development is a separate extensibility topic
knowledgeItems.summary: Atozed has dedicated IntraWeb 17 material for custom controls. Extensibility should therefore be represented as its own information and posting branch.

knowledgeItems.title: Code behind is a distinct interface/logic separation topic
knowledgeItems.summary: The documentation structure contains Code Behind as a distinct concept, useful for explaining where interface description ends and application logic begins.

knowledgeItems.title: Web-server setup deserves its own operational branch
knowledgeItems.summary: The IW17 documentation includes web-server setup such as Apache configuration. Installation/server setup should remain separate from authoring and deployment topics.

knowledgeItems.title: Content idea: first IW17 project from VS Code
knowledgeItems.summary: Short walkthrough: choose JS or TS, create the project, explain the four generated file types, then run it. This directly follows the current extension documentation.

knowledgeItems.title: Content idea: create a new IW17 page and launch it
knowledgeItems.summary: Show New Page, generated files, automatic launch.json update and immediate run/debug. This is a concrete short-form workflow from the current docs.

knowledgeItems.title: Content idea: designer and IWML source are two views of the same page
knowledgeItems.summary: Demonstrate opening the same IWML visually and as text to explain that visual authoring does not remove source ownership.

knowledgeItems.title: Content idea: IWML as a DFM-like web page description
knowledgeItems.summary: Explain the documented DFM analogy, then show how IWCL turns the IWML structure into browser HTML.

knowledgeItems.title: Content idea: one-way vs two-way binding with REST
knowledgeItems.summary: Use a minimal example to show the difference between one-way and two-way binding and how a REST-backed source fits the same binding model.

knowledgeItems.title: Content idea: IWML Runner vs web-server execution
knowledgeItems.summary: Compare the two documented run paths and when each one is useful during development.

knowledgeItems.title: Content idea: put an IW17 block inside WordPress
knowledgeItems.summary: Use the current product-page Custom HTML flow as a visual before/after demo from designer to a live WordPress section.

knowledgeItems.title: Content idea: what “small project footprint” actually means in the official Guess comparison
knowledgeItems.summary: Explain files, folders, dependencies and output ownership using the official product-page numbers, while clearly labeling them as Atozed’s example.

knowledgeItems.title: Content idea: what IntraWeb 17 One removes from the FE/BE workflow
knowledgeItems.summary: Visualize the glue/API/integration steps the product page says IntraWeb One is intended to automate between frontend and backend.

knowledgeItems.title: Content idea: build offline and keep the output
knowledgeItems.summary: Show the product claim as a practical workflow: VS Code, local project, native debugging, source control and developer-owned output.

knowledgeItems.title: Comparison rule: verify the competing setup before publishing
knowledgeItems.summary: The official product page provides React, Vue and Angular comparison examples, but external comparison content should re-check equivalent current competitor versions and setup before making a claim.

knowledgeItems.title: Watch frontend build-tool and dependency complexity as context
knowledgeItems.summary: Track current build tooling, dependency and packaging changes only to contextualize verified IW17 facts. Do not let market-watch material overwrite the official product knowledge tree.
